title: BENICAR (olmesartan medoxomil) tablets, for oral use: full prescribing information
journal: US Food and Drug Administration-approved labelling, published in DailyMed (National Library of Medicine); structured product label version 1, effective 23 September 2025
funder: not stated. The document is prescribing information approved by the US Food and Drug Administration and published by the labeller, Cosette Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
result: Warning 5.5, sprue-like enteropathy: severe, chronic diarrhoea with substantial weight loss has been reported months to years after starting olmesartan; intestinal biopsies often showed villous atrophy; if no other cause is found, alternative antihypertensive therapy is to be considered. Post-marketing reports include angio-oedema, anaphylactic reactions, hyperkalaemia, rhabdomyolysis and acute renal failure. In the placebo-controlled ROADMAP trial (n=4447) of olmesartan 40 mg daily in type 2 diabetes with normoalbuminuria, onset of microalbuminuria was delayed but decline in GFR was not slowed, and adjudicated cardiovascular death occurred in 15 on olmesartan against 3 on placebo (hazard ratio 4.9, 95% CI 1.4 to 17). In an epidemiological study of patients aged 65 or older with over 300,000 patient-years of exposure, diabetic patients taking 40 mg/day for more than 6 months had a higher risk of death than those on other angiotensin receptor blockers (hazard ratio 2.0, 1.1 to 3.8), whereas non-diabetic patients had a lower risk (0.46, 0.24 to 0.86); the label states that the data raise a concern of possible increased cardiovascular risk with high-dose olmesartan in diabetes but are not conclusive.
